name: green-level-input-history-offset
note: `close[r]` where `r` is an input, not a literal. OS2006 required a literal history offset, which is what put Pine's `volume[liqRightLen]` -- the volume AT the pivot bar -- out of reach and left the ICT suite's `EQH (8.8M)` labels unportable. An INPUT is constant for the whole run, so this is a fixed shift the planner can bound by `maxval`, not a per-bar-varying offset; warmup is priced at the declared bound. Here r defaults to 2 and the level spawns at bar 3, so its price must be close[2] counted back from bar 3 = close at bar 1 = 8.5. Picking up the spawn bar's own close (12) or bar 2's (10.75) are the two off-by-one failures this pins.
source:
indicator("H", shorttitle="H", overlay=true)
r = input.int(2, "R", minval=0, maxval=10)
plotlevel(bar_index == 3, close[r], "L", extend=extend.bars, bars=1)
